CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFPROCPARAM

Each CFPROCPARAM inside a CFSTOREDPROC supplies one parameter. Without DBVARNAME the parameters are matched to the procedure's parameters in the order the procedure declares them; with DBVARNAME they are matched by name. Input parameters carry a value; output parameters name a CFML variable that receives the procedure's value when the call returns.

Category

Database manipulation

Syntax

<CFPROCPARAM TYPE="In/Out/InOut"
    VARIABLE="variable_name"
    DBVARNAME="db_variable_name"
    VALUE="parameter_value"
    CFSQLTYPE="parameter_datatype"
    MAXLENGTH="length"
    SCALE="decimal_places"
    NULL="Yes/No">

Attributes

TYPE
Optional, default "In". In passes a value, Out receives one, InOut does both.
VARIABLE
Required for Out and InOut. CFML variable that receives the output value. A NULL comes back as an empty string, a date as "yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss", like the columns of a query.
DBVARNAME
Optional. Name of the parameter in the procedure, such as @Department, to bind by name instead of by position. Positional parameters must come before named ones.
VALUE
Required for In and InOut. The value to pass. It is checked against CFSQLTYPE before the call.
CFSQLTYPE
Required. CF_SQL_BIGINT, CF_SQL_BIT, CF_SQL_CHAR, CF_SQL_DATE, CF_SQL_DECIMAL, CF_SQL_DOUBLE, CF_SQL_FLOAT, CF_SQL_IDSTAMP, CF_SQL_INTEGER, CF_SQL_LONGVARCHAR, CF_SQL_MONEY, CF_SQL_MONEY4, CF_SQL_NUMERIC, CF_SQL_REAL, CF_SQL_REFCURSOR, CF_SQL_SMALLINT, CF_SQL_TIME, CF_SQL_TIMESTAMP, CF_SQL_TINYINT or CF_SQL_VARCHAR. CF_SQL_REFCURSOR (Oracle cursors) is refused by the flat-file driver, which returns result sets directly.
MAXLENGTH
Optional. Maximum length of an input value (longer values throw an exception) and of a returned string.
SCALE
Optional. Decimal places a returned numeric value is rounded to.
NULL
Optional, default "No". Yes passes SQL NULL and ignores VALUE.

Usage

The procedure converts each value to the type it declares: a VARCHAR(5) parameter keeps five characters, an INT drops the fraction, and a value that does not convert ends the call with "Conversion failed when converting ...". Leave out a parameter that has a default, or bind it by name and skip it.

A procedure parameter must be declared OUTPUT for a TYPE="Out" or "InOut" CFPROCPARAM; otherwise the call fails with "The formal parameter ... was not declared as an OUTPUT parameter".

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- AddEmployee returns the new Emp_ID in an output parameter and a status code:
      0 = added, 1 = no such department, 2 = already on file.
      The transaction is rolled back, so the sample data stays the same. --->
<CFTRANSACTION>
  <CFSTOREDPROC PROCEDURE="AddEmployee" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets" RETURNCODE="Yes">
    <CFPROCPARAM TYPE="In" CFSQLTYPE="CF_SQL_VARCHAR" DBVARNAME="@FirstName" VALUE="Wendy">
    <CFPROCPARAM TYPE="In" CFSQLTYPE="CF_SQL_VARCHAR" DBVARNAME="@LastName" VALUE="Okonkwo">
    <CFPROCPARAM TYPE="In" CFSQLTYPE="CF_SQL_VARCHAR" DBVARNAME="@Department" VALUE="Training">
    <CFPROCPARAM TYPE="In" CFSQLTYPE="CF_SQL_MONEY" DBVARNAME="@Salary" VALUE="42500">
    <CFPROCPARAM TYPE="Out" CFSQLTYPE="CF_SQL_INTEGER" DBVARNAME="@NewID" VARIABLE="NewID">
  </CFSTOREDPROC>
  <CFSET Status = CFSTOREDPROC.StatusCode>
  <CFQUERY NAME="Added" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
  SELECT FirstName, LastName, Department, Salary FROM Employees WHERE Emp_ID = #NewID#
  </CFQUERY>
  <CFTRANSACTION ACTION="Rollback"/>
</CFTRANSACTION>

<CFOUTPUT>
<P>Status #Status#: employee number #NewID# is
#Added.FirstName# #Added.LastName# (#Added.Department#, #DollarFormat(Added.Salary)#).</P>
</CFOUTPUT>
